reason: Both conversations gave the correct critical safety boundary (switch off at the consumer unit, don't touch the plug/extension lead while wet) and both correctly identified the Fairy liquid as the cause with no part needed. Conversation 2 edged ahead by explicitly redirecting the 'should i just pull the plug' request to the fuse box, spotting the foam cause a turn earlier, and finishing with practical next steps: mop up safely, have the wetted sockets/extension lead checked by an electrician, and tell the landlord. Conversation 1 asked a less relevant first question (water in the base), ended with an awkward unfinished offer ('Once we know that, I can guide you...') and no actionable guidance on clearing the floor or suds, and never mentioned the landlord. Conversation 2 is held back by its speculative first-turn list of door-seal/hose/spray-arm causes and a repetitive third turn, and both over-escalate by saying the dishwasher itself needs an engineer, so the margin is only slight.
